The Grand Challenge

Mix It Up!

Booth 1 · Ring Toss
Let's Learn!

What Is Addition?

Addition means putting two groups together to make ONE bigger group. When you add, the total always gets BIGGER!

← Review the lesson

How Many Friends Are Coming?

Tap each peg to toss a ring! First collect Group A, then Group B, and watch the total grow.

? + ? = ?
Booth 2 · Stack the Crates
Let's Learn!

Tens and Ones

Big numbers are made of TENS and ONES. A ten is like a bundle of 10 little ones stuck together. The number 23 means 2 tens and 3 ones!

← Review the lesson

Boxes of Cups

Cups come in crates of 10! Tap each crate and box to stack it on the scale.

Tens: 0 | Ones: 0 | Total: 0
Booth 3 · Whack-a-Mole
Let's Learn!

What Is Subtraction?

Subtraction means taking some away from a group. When you subtract, the total always gets SMALLER!

← Review the lesson

Some Friends Are Sick

12 friends were coming, but 4 are sick today. Whack exactly 4 moles to send them home!

12 friends coming
Booth 4 · Dart Throw
Let's Learn!

Subtracting Bigger Numbers

Subtracting big numbers works just the same as small ones — you're still taking some away and counting what's left!

← Review the lesson

Popping Used Balloons

We started with 30 balloons. Tap the wall 12 times to pop the ones already used!

30 balloons
Booth 5 · Magician's Hat
Let's Learn!

Now You See It...

Sometimes we know the TOTAL but not one of the parts. If the magician has 8 bunnies and shows you 5, you can figure out how many are hiding — that's a missing-number puzzle!

← Review the lesson

Now You See It, Now You Don't!

The magician has some bunnies under his hat!

Trick 1 of 4
Booth 6 · Strongman Hammer
Let's Learn!

What Is Multiplication?

Multiplication is a FAST way to add the same number again and again. Instead of 4 + 4 + 4, we just say 3 × 4!

← Review the lesson

Light Up 3 Rows of 4!

Test your strength! Tap the hammer to light up the game booths, one row of 4 at a time.

0 rows of 4 = 0
Booth 7 · Lily Pad Hop
Let's Learn!

What Is Skip-Counting?

Skip-counting means jumping by the SAME amount every time — like hopping by 5s: 5... 10... 15... 20! It's really multiplication in disguise.

← Review the lesson

Skip-Count to Set Up Chairs

Chairs come in stacks of 5! Tap to hop along the lily pads and skip-count by 5s.

0 chairs
Booth 8 · Duck Pond
Let's Learn!

What Is Division? (Sharing)

Division means splitting one big group into EQUAL smaller groups, so everyone gets a fair share!

← Review the lesson

Sharing the Lemonade

Tap a duck to catch it, then tap a boat to place it. Share all 12 cups evenly among 4 boats!

Ducks left to place: 12
Booth 9 · Team Huddle
Let's Learn!

Division: Making Groups

Division can also mean counting how many equal-sized groups you can make from one big group!

← Review the lesson

Making Relay Teams

Tap each kid to send them to the next huddle. Every team needs exactly 3!

Kids left: 15
Booth 10 · Fortune Teller's Tent
Let's Learn!

What Is Estimating?

Estimating means making a smart GUESS without counting one by one. It's a real math superpower — great mathematicians estimate before they calculate!

← Review the lesson

Gaze Into the Crystal Ball!

About how many stars do you see? Don't count one by one — take a quick guess!

Guess 1 of 3
Booth 11 · Wheel of Word Problems
Let's Learn!

Picking the Right Tool

Every math story has clue words! "In all" or "altogether" usually means ADD. "Left" usually means SUBTRACT. Let's practice spotting the clues!

← Review the lesson

Which Operation?

Spin the wheel, then pick add, subtract, multiply, or divide!

Booth 12 · The Journey
Let's Learn!

Taking a Math Journey

Some math stories have MANY steps. We solve them one step at a time, in the same order they happen — just like walking down a path!

← Review the lesson

Melissa's Chocolate Journey

Tap "Start" to begin the journey!

Booth 13 · Pizza Party
Let's Learn!

What Is a Fraction?

A fraction shows part of a whole thing, like part of a pizza. The BOTTOM number counts all the equal slices. The TOP number counts how many YOU have.

← Review the lesson

Splitting the Pizza

Tap slices to "eat" them. Try to eat exactly HALF the pizza!
